Build and Evaluate Explicit Lexical-Diversity Method Plans

lexdiv_profile.Rd

Builds bounded, reproducible plans for computing multiple parameter settings of the versioned lexical-diversity methods without changing the established canonical API. The identity hierarchy is metric family, versioned method, and normalized method-plus-parameter specification.

Usage

lexdiv_spec(method_id, parameters = list(), request_id = NULL)

lexdiv_grid(
  method_id,
  parameter,
  values,
  request_id_prefix = NULL,
  max_values = 128L
)

lexdiv_plan(
  presets = "canonical",
  specs = list(),
  grids = list(),
  max_specs = 128L
)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_spec'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_grid'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_plan'
print(x, ...)

lexdiv_methods()

lexdiv_presets()

lexdiv_profile(tokens, plan = lexdiv_plan())

lexdiv_profile_batch(
  documents,
  plan = lexdiv_plan(),
  id_col = "document_id",
  tokens_col = "tokens",
  max_rows = 1e6
)

lexdiv_screen(
  x,
  floors = c(tokens_50 = 50L, tokens_100 = 100L),
  max_rows = 2e+06
)

Arguments

method_id

One versioned method identifier returned by lexdiv_methods(). A method fixes its formula, scale, boundary, tail, and aggregation rules.

parameters

A plain named list of user-settable method parameters. Omitted values are materialized from the versioned defaults.

request_id

An optional plain ASCII identifier used to join one request to its profile result.

parameter

The one user-settable scalar parameter admitted by the selected current method.

values

A non-empty numeric vector whose elements become distinct method specifications after validation and normalization.

request_id_prefix

An optional ASCII prefix for the one-based request IDs generated by lexdiv_grid().

max_values

A positive integer bound on values expanded eagerly by one grid call. Raise it explicitly only when that allocation is intentional.

presets

A duplicate-free plain character vector selected from lexdiv_presets(). Use character() for a custom-only plan.

specs

One lexdiv_spec, or a plain list of such objects, appended after preset requests.

grids

One lexdiv_grid, or a plain list of such objects, appended after explicit specifications.

max_specs

A positive integer bound on the number of distinct normalized specifications in a plan.

tokens

One pre-tokenized document accepted by lexdiv_metrics().

plan

A normalized request plan returned by lexdiv_plan().

documents

A named list or data frame/list-column input accepted by lexdiv_metrics_batch().

id_col

The explicit document-ID column name for data-frame input.

tokens_col

The token-vector list-column name for data-frame input.

max_rows

A positive integer output bound, checked before computation or allocation. For lexdiv_profile_batch() it bounds document-by-specification rows; for lexdiv_screen() it bounds source-row-by-floor rows.

x

For print(), a specification, grid, or plan returned by the corresponding constructor. For lexdiv_screen(), a result returned by lexdiv_profile() or lexdiv_profile_batch().

floors

A non-empty named numeric vector of positive integer token-count screens. Names become screen_id; values become minimum_tokens.

...

Additional arguments passed to print.data.frame().

Value

lexdiv_spec() returns a normalized lexdiv_spec; lexdiv_grid() returns an ordered list of specifications; lexdiv_plan() returns a deduplicated lexdiv_plan with an MD5 fingerprint over normalized request identity and order. Their print methods return the input invisibly after displaying a bounded tabular view; the full identity fields remain available on the object.

lexdiv_methods() returns a metadata data frame with human-readable labels and definitions, stability (including experimental expected-TTR D), conventional within-method direction, contract scale, exact method identity, parameters, and advisory token floors. lexdiv_presets() returns a preset metadata data frame. lexdiv_profile() returns one core metric row per plan request with a separate profile envelope. lexdiv_profile_batch() adds the existing batch envelope and returns document-major, request-minor long form.

lexdiv_screen() returns a lexdiv_screen_results data frame with one row per source result and named floor. It deliberately has no metric-value column.

Details

Preset version 0.2.0 excludes experimental expected-TTR D. The canonical preset contains eleven methods at their default parameters. The length_50_100 preset adds MSTTR at segment length 100 and MATTR at window length 100. It has thirteen specifications: MTLD is computed only once because a 50- versus 100-token quality screen does not change its calculation.

Saved core-contract 0.1.0 plans must be recreated explicitly; see the migration section in lexdiv_metrics. An explicitly constructed lexdiv_spec("expected_ttr_d_hypergeom_fit_v1") still selects the experimental estimator.

Duplicate normalized method/parameter specifications from presets, explicit specifications, or grids collapse at their first position. Distinct remaining specifications must have distinct request IDs. Parameter grids form an ordered union, not a cross-product across metrics. Requested limits are checked before a large result is allocated. Independently of max_specs, a plan rejects more than 1,024 raw preset, explicit-specification, and expanded-grid candidates before normalization; this prevents an arbitrarily large duplicate input from bypassing the distinct-specification bound.

The specification, grid, and plan print methods show request, metric, method, and parameter identity without dumping the internal canonical identity string. Long vector parameters are abbreviated for display only. Printing never changes or truncates the stored object.

Profile rows make the method's advisory default floor explicit as default_quality_floor_tokens. Independently requested screens are non-censoring: they do not change a metric value, effective parameter, status, or document membership. A 50- or 100-token screen is therefore not an MTLD method variant, and truncating a document to one of those lengths would be a separate sampling design. Passing a screen does not establish measurement validity, reliability, proficiency, or writing quality; failing one does not invalidate an otherwise computable metric row.

The profile and screen schemas are distinct from the core metric and batch schemas. Third-party implementation names are not compatibility presets; such a preset requires an exact, version-pinned method contract and boundary fixtures.

Examples

methods <- lexdiv_methods()
lexdiv_presets()
#>       preset_id preset_version specification_count
#> 1     canonical          0.2.0                  11
#> 2 length_50_100          0.2.0                  13
#>                                              description
#> 1 The eleven stable methods at their canonical defaults.
#> 2          Canonical plus MSTTR and MATTR at length 100.
mattr_method <- methods$method_id[methods$metric_id == "mattr"]

mattr_25 <- lexdiv_spec(
  mattr_method,
  parameters = list(window_length = 25),
  request_id = "mattr_25"
)

grid <- lexdiv_grid(
  mattr_method,
  parameter = "window_length",
  values = c(50, 100),
  request_id_prefix = "mattr"
)
plan <- lexdiv_plan(presets = character(), specs = mattr_25, grids = grid)
print(mattr_25)
#> <lexdiv_spec: mattr-c60bcc139197f0321525ede59195f383>
#>  request_id metric_id              method_id       parameters
#>    mattr_25     mattr mattr_sliding_step1_v1 window_length=25
print(grid)
#> <lexdiv_grid: 2 specifications>
#>  request_index request_id metric_id              method_id        parameters
#>              1    mattr_1     mattr mattr_sliding_step1_v1  window_length=50
#>              2    mattr_2     mattr mattr_sliding_step1_v1 window_length=100
print(plan)
#> <lexdiv_plan: 3 specifications; schema 0.1.0; id 385893509c8011275b045ea68daa5cb9>
#>  request_index request_id metric_id              method_id        parameters
#>              1   mattr_25     mattr mattr_sliding_step1_v1  window_length=25
#>              2    mattr_1     mattr mattr_sliding_step1_v1  window_length=50
#>              3    mattr_2     mattr mattr_sliding_step1_v1 window_length=100

tokens <- rep(c("a", "b", "a", "c", "d"), 25)
profile <- lexdiv_profile(tokens, plan)
profile[, c("request_id", "metric_id", "value", "status")]
#> <lexdiv_profile_results: 3 specifications; schema unknown>
#>   request_id metric_id value status
#> 1   mattr_25     mattr  0.16     ok
#> 2    mattr_1     mattr  0.08     ok
#> 3    mattr_2     mattr  0.04     ok

screens <- lexdiv_screen(profile)
screens[, c("request_id", "screen_id", "minimum_tokens", "passes_screen")]
#>   request_id  screen_id minimum_tokens passes_screen
#> 1   mattr_25  tokens_50             50          TRUE
#> 2   mattr_25 tokens_100            100          TRUE
#> 3    mattr_1  tokens_50             50          TRUE
#> 4    mattr_1 tokens_100            100          TRUE
#> 5    mattr_2  tokens_50             50          TRUE
#> 6    mattr_2 tokens_100            100          TRUE

documents <- list(document_a = tokens, document_b = rev(tokens))
batch_profile <- lexdiv_profile_batch(documents, plan)
head(batch_profile[, c("document_id", "request_id", "metric_id", "status")])
#> <lexdiv_profile_batch_results: 2 documents; 6 specification results; schema unknown>
#>   document_id request_id metric_id status
#> 1  document_a   mattr_25     mattr     ok
#> 2  document_a    mattr_1     mattr     ok
#> 3  document_a    mattr_2     mattr     ok
#> 4  document_b   mattr_25     mattr     ok
#> 5  document_b    mattr_1     mattr     ok
#> 6  document_b    mattr_2     mattr     ok

all_lengths <- lexdiv_plan("length_50_100")
length(all_lengths$specifications)
#> [1] 13
